drills.title: Whose Job Is It?
drills.description: A task lands on the scene. Toss it to the right vest — fast. Wrong vest = lost minutes.

items.prompt: Sending the METHANE report and naming the incident.
items.why: Command owns the first report and naming the incident.

items.prompt: Shouting 'If you can walk, come to the blue tent!'
items.why: Global sort is the triage officer's opening move.

items.prompt: Choosing which hospital gets the next red patient.
items.why: Transport matches patients to hospital capability and capacity.

items.prompt: Laying out red, yellow, and green tarps.
items.why: Treatment Officer sets up the treatment area.

items.prompt: Making mutual-aid ambulances check in, keys left in the ignition.
items.why: Staging tracks and holds available vehicles.

items.prompt: Stopping a crew from walking under a sagging roof.
items.why: Safety Officer can stop unsafe acts immediately.

items.prompt: Applying a tourniquet in 10 seconds then moving on.
items.why: Seconds-long LSIs are allowed during triage.
The transport log is the Transport Officer's record.

items.prompt: Requesting 6 more ambulances and a bus from dispatch.
Secondary triage of patients arriving at the treatment area.
items.why: Treatment re-triages on entry to the treatment area.

items.prompt: Telling the IC 'only 2 ambulances left available'.
items.why: Staging reports when available resources drop to the trigger level.

items.prompt: Reporting '5 red, 9 yellow, 21 green, 2 black' to command.
items.why: Triage owns the casualty count by category.

items.prompt: Coordinating with police and fire chiefs at one command post.
items.why: Unified command coordination is a command function.

items.prompt: Calling the next ambulance up from staging to the loading zone.
items.why: Transport requests units from staging as patients are ready.

items.prompt: Enforcing respiratory protection near a smoldering chemical drum.
items.why: PPE and hazard enforcement are safety functions.
